results.fact: pitch count on the South Ridge
results.summary: The newest book calls the South Ridge a three-pitch climb, but the row's whole rappel descent is built on a four-segment division, so changing the header alone would create a new contradiction.
results.evidence: selectedclimbsin0000nels (2003) p78: "the three-pitch South Ridge"; p81 route: red slab via cracks (5.2) to a large ledge, a short pitch to the base of the upper slab, crack and face to another broken ledge, then the west side of the crest to the summit. cascadealpinegui0000beck (2000 ed., vol. 1 Columbia R.-Stevens Pass) p319 describes the same line (40 ft crack 5.2 to a horn belay; slab-centre crack 5.4 to a ledge with two fixed pitons "(optional belay)"; a short class-4 pitch; scramble to the summit) without a pitch count, i.e. 3 or 4 depending on the optional belay. The row: pitches 4; pitch_detail 3 rows; waypoints and itinerary say 3 pitches; but rappels, descent, descent_text, rappel_detail and rappel_count_note all describe four single-rope rappels "one per pitch", with stations named "top of pitch 3/2/1" below a summit pitch. Setting pitches 3 would leave rappel_detail rappel 1 ("down the uppermost pitch to the top of pitch 3") contradicting it, and the book gives no rappel layout to rewrite those stations from. Owner decision: adopt 3 and rewrite the four rappel stations' pitch labels, or keep 4. rockclimbingwash0000smoo has no Ingalls entry.
searched: cascadealpinegui0000beck (2000 ed., vol. 1 Columbia R.-Stevens Pass): "Chimney Rock" "South Peak" (returned the Ingalls South Ridge p317-319 text)
